answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work; a public atlas records the lock and links each claim to a unique deposit. Once per pulse, randomly selected peers audit a sample, and a proven duplicate identity forfeits its stake. A plume of fake accounts therefore cannot cheaply multiply voting or rewards: the attacker must fund every identity and risks losing those funds when audits expose coordinated behavior. The mechanism raises the cost of Sybils, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prove that distinct stakes belong to distinct people.
